study type: Prospective Cohort Study with a diagnostic accuracy component
cohort: The study included 822 women who had undergone a vaginal delivery.
finding: Clinical examination by abdominal palpation demonstrated limited sensitivity (66.1%) for diagnosing postpartum urinary retention, which was significantly associated with longer labor duration and increased VAS scores.
cross-section timing: Postnatal period after vaginal delivery, unspecified timing
